passages.text: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him.
passages.sermon:
The Passover was two days away.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread was also two days away.
The chief priests wanted to arrest Jesus.
The scribes also wanted to arrest Jesus.
They looked for a secret way to take hold of Jesus.
They planned to kill Him.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὰ ἄζυμα μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς πῶς αὐτὸν ἐν δόλῳ κρατήσαντες ἀποκτείνωσιν

passages.text: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the scribes wanted to arrest Jesus secretly.
They wanted to kill Him.
They said, “Not during the feast.”
They feared a riot among the people.
passages.original: ἔλεγον γάρ Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ μή‿ ποτε ἔσται θόρυβος τοῦ λαοῦ

passages.text: While Jesus was in Bethany reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus’ head.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in Bethany.
He was at the house of Simon the Leper.
Jesus was reclining at the table.
A woman came to Him.
She brought an alabaster jar.
The jar contained expensive perfume.
The perfume was made of pure nard.
She broke open the jar.
She poured the perfume on Jesus’ head.
passages.original: Καὶ ὄντος αὐτοῦ ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ κατακειμένου αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτελοῦς συντρίψασα τὴν ἀλάβαστρον κατέχεεν αὐτοῦ τῆς κεφαλῆς

passages.text: Some of those present, however, expressed their indignation to one another: “Why this waste of perfume?
passages.sermon:
Some people were present with Jesus.
These people felt angry.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “Why was this perfume wasted?”
passages.original: Ἦσαν δέ τινες ἀγανακτοῦντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη τοῦ μύρου γέγονεν

passages.text: It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.
passages.sermon:
Some people were present with Jesus in Simon’s house.
They saw the woman pour perfume on Jesus’ head.
They became angry with her.
They said, “This perfume could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii.”
They said, “The money could have been given to the poor.”
They scolded the woman.
passages.original: ἠδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο τὸ μύρον πραθῆναι ἐπάνω δηναρίων τριακοσίων καὶ δοθῆναι τοῖς πτωχοῖς καὶ ἐνεβριμῶντο αὐτῇ

passages.text: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, “Leave this woman alone.
Do not trouble her.
She has done a good work for Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἄφετε αὐτήν τί αὐτῇ κόπους παρέχετε καλὸν ἔργον ἠργάσατο ἐν ἐμοί

passages.text: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you will not always have Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You will always have poor people with you.
You can help the poor whenever you want.
But you will not always have Me with you.”
passages.original: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν καὶ ὅταν θέλητε δύνασθε αὐτοῖς εὖ ποιῆσαι ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε

passages.text: She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the woman.
She did what she could.
She anointed My body.
She did this before My burial.
passages.original: ὃ ἔσχεν ἐποίησεν προέλαβεν μυρίσαι τὸ σῶμά μου εἰς τὸν ἐνταφιασμόν

passages.text: And truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
People will preach the gospel in all the world.
Wherever people preach the gospel, they will also tell what this woman has done.
They will remember her by telling about her actions.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη λαληθήσεται εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς

passages.text: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.
passages.sermon: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.\r\nJudas went to the chief priests.\r\nJudas wanted to betray Jesus to the chief priests.
passages.original: Καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριὼθ ὁ εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδοῖ αὐτοῖς

passages.text: They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests heard Judas.
They felt great joy.
They promised to give Judas money.
Judas began to look for a good time to betray Jesus.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐχάρησαν καὶ ἐπηγγείλαντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι καὶ ἐζήτει πῶς αὐτὸν εὐκαίρως παραδοῖ

passages.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked Him, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a teacher.
He had disciples.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread began.
This was the first day of the feast.
On this day, people sacrificed the Passover lamb.
Jesus’ disciples spoke to Him.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Where do You want us to go?”
They wanted to prepare for Jesus to eat the Passover meal.
passages.original: Καὶ τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν ἀζύμων ὅτε τὸ πάσχα ἔθυον λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ Ποῦ θέλεις ἀπελθόντες ἑτοιμάσωμεν ἵνα φάγῃς τὸ πάσχα

passages.text: So He sent two of His disciples and told them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him, and whichever house he enters, say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus chose two of His disciples.
Jesus sent these two disciples on a task.
Jesus told them, “Go into the city.”
Jesus said, “You will meet a man there.”
This man will be carrying a jug of water.
Jesus said, “Follow this man.”
Jesus said, “Watch which house he enters.”
Jesus told them, “Go into that house.”
Jesus said, “Speak to the owner of the house.”
Jesus told them to say, “The Teacher asks a question.”
Jesus told them to say, “Where is My guest room?”
Jesus told them to say, “I want to eat the Passover there with My disciples.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ εἴπατε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅτι Ὁ Διδάσκαλος λέγει Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμά μου ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω

passages.text: And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to two of His disciples.
He told them about a man they would meet in the city.
This man would show them a large upper room.
The room would be furnished.
The room would be ready.
Jesus told the disciples to prepare the Passover meal there for Him and His disciples.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον ἕτοιμον καὶ ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν

passages.text: So the disciples left and went into the city, where they found everything as Jesus had described. And they prepared the Passover.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them what to do.
The disciples obeyed Jesus.
They left.
They went into the city.
They found everything just as Jesus had said.
They prepared the Passover meal.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα

passages.text: When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the teacher and leader of the disciples.
The Twelve are His closest followers.
Evening came.
Jesus arrived.
The Twelve disciples came with Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα

passages.text: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
They were reclining at the table.
They were eating together.
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “Truly I tell you.”
He said, “One of you will betray Me.”
He said, “This person is eating with Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀνακειμένων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσθιόντων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με ὁ ἐσθίων μετ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: They began to be grieved and to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples sat with Jesus.
Jesus told them that one of them would betray Him.
Each disciple felt sad.
Each disciple asked Jesus a question.
Each disciple said, “Surely not I?”
passages.original: ἤρξαντο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς κατὰ εἷς Μήτι ἐγώ

passages.text: He answered, “It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, "One of you will betray Me."
This person is one of the Twelve disciples.
He is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ὁ ἐμβαπτόμενος μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὸ τρύβλιον

passages.text: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
God wrote about the Son of Man in the Scriptures.
The Son of Man will go as the Scriptures say.
Someone will betray the Son of Man.
Woe to that man who betrays Him.
It would be better for that man if he had not been born.
passages.original: ὅτι ὁ μὲν Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται καλὸν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος

passages.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take it; this is My body.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was eating with His disciples.
He took bread.
He spoke a blessing over the bread.
He broke the bread.
He gave the bread to His disciples.
He said, “Take it.
This is My body.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν Λάβετε τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου

passages.text: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat with His disciples.
He took a cup.
He gave thanks to God.
He gave the cup to His disciples.
All of the disciples drank from the cup.
passages.original: Καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἔπιον ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες

passages.text: He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “This is My blood.”
This blood belongs to the covenant.
My blood is poured out for many people.
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ ἐκχυννόμενον ὑπὲρ πολλῶν

passages.text: Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
I will not drink from the fruit of the vine again.
I will wait until that day comes.
On that day, I will drink it new.
I will drink it in the kingdom of God.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἐκ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples finished their meal.
They sang a hymn together.
They left the place where they ate.
They went out to the Mount of Olives.
passages.original: Καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “All of you will fall away.”
Scripture says, “I will strike the Shepherd.”
The sheep will scatter.
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πάντες σκανδαλισθήσεσθε ὅτι γέγραπται Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα Καὶ τὰ πρόβατα διασκορπισθήσονται

passages.text: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said He would rise from the dead.
After He rose, He would go ahead of them.
He would go to Galilee before them.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν

passages.text: Peter declared, “Even if all fall away, I never will.”
passages.sermon: Peter was a disciple of Jesus.\r\nPeter spoke to Jesus.\r\nPeter said, “Even if everyone else falls away, I will not fall away.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἔφη αὐτῷ Εἰ καὶ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγώ

passages.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
Tonight, this very night, you will deny Me three times.
You will do this before the rooster crows twice.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι σὺ σήμερον ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἢ δὶς ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ

passages.text: But Peter kept insisting, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the others said the same thing.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter spoke very strongly.
Peter said, “Even if I must die with You, I will not deny You.”
All the other disciples said the same thing.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐκπερισσῶς ἐλάλει Ἐὰν δέῃ με συναποθανεῖν σοι οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ πάντες ἔλεγον

passages.text: Then they came to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus told His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
They traveled together to a place.
The name of the place was Gethsemane.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Sit here.”
He said, “I will pray.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς χωρίον οὗ τὸ ὄνομα Γεθσημανί καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Καθίσατε ὧδε ἕως προσεύξωμαι

passages.text: He took with Him Peter, James, and John, and began to be deeply troubled and distressed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus took Peter with Him.
Jesus took James with Him.
Jesus took John with Him.
Jesus began to feel deeply troubled.
Jesus began to feel distressed.
passages.original: καὶ παραλαμβάνει τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤρξατο ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν

passages.text: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter, James, and John.
He said, “My soul is very sad.
I am sorrowful to the point of death.
Stay here.
Keep watch.”
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε

passages.text: Going a little farther, He fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour would pass from Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
\r\nJesus felt deep sorrow and distress.
\r\nJesus walked a little farther away from His disciples.
\r\nJesus fell to the ground.
\r\nJesus prayed.
\r\nJesus asked God if it was possible for the coming hour of suffering to pass from Him.
passages.original: Καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπιπτεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ προσηύχετο ἵνα εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν παρέλθῃ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἡ ὥρα

passages.text: “Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to God the Father.
He called God “Abba, Father.”
Jesus said that God can do all things.
Jesus asked God to take the cup away from Him.
Jesus did not want His own will.
Jesus wanted God’s will to be done.
passages.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν Ἀββᾶ ὁ Πατήρ πάντα δυνατά σοι παρένεγκε τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ ἀλλ’ οὐ τί ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλὰ τί σύ

passages.text: Then Jesus returned and found them sleeping. “Simon, are you asleep?” He asked. “Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus returned to His disciples.
He found the disciples sleeping.
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus called Peter by his other name, Simon.
Jesus asked Simon, “Are you asleep?”
Jesus asked Simon, “Could you not keep watch for one hour?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχεται καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ Σίμων καθεύδεις οὐκ ἴσχυσας μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι

passages.text: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to watch.
He told them to pray.
He said this would keep them from entering into temptation.
He explained that the spirit is willing.
He also explained that the body is weak.
passages.original: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε ἵνα μὴ ἔλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής

passages.text: Again He went away and prayed, saying the same thing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left the disciples again.
He went away from them.
He prayed.
He spoke the same words as before.
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπών

passages.text: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping—for their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to answer Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus returned again.
He found the disciples sleeping.
Their eyes felt very heavy.
They did not know what to say to Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ πάλιν ἐλθὼν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καταβαρυνόμενοι καὶ οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τί ἀποκριθῶσιν αὐτῷ

passages.text: When Jesus returned the third time, He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? That is enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus returned to His disciples a third time.
He spoke to them.
He said, "Are you still sleeping?"
He said, "Are you still resting?"
He said, "That is enough."
He said, "The hour has come."
He said, "Look."
He said, "The Son of Man is betrayed."
He said, "He is handed over into the hands of sinners."
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχεται τὸ τρίτον καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε ἀπέχει ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα ἰδοὺ παραδίδοται ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν

passages.text: Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Get up.
Let us go.
Look.
The one who will betray Me is coming.”
passages.original: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν ἰδοὺ ὁ παραδιδούς με ἤγγικεν

passages.text: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was still speaking.
Judas arrived.
Judas was one of the Twelve disciples.
A crowd came with Judas.
The crowd carried swords and clubs.
The chief priests sent the crowd.
The scribes sent the crowd.
The elders sent the crowd.
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος παραγίνεται ὁ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων

passages.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.”
passages.sermon:
Judas was the betrayer of Jesus.
Judas made a secret signal with the men who came to arrest Jesus.
Judas told them, “The man I kiss is the one you must arrest.”
Judas said, “Take hold of Him and lead Him away safely.”
passages.original: Δεδώκει δὲ ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν σύσσημον αὐτοῖς λέγων Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν κρατήσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπάγετε ἀσφαλῶς

passages.text: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
passages.sermon:
Judas was one of the Twelve disciples.
Judas went straight to Jesus.
Judas said, “Rabbi!” to Jesus.
Judas kissed Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εὐθὺς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ λέγει Ῥαββί καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν

passages.text: Then the men seized Jesus and arrested Him.
passages.sermon:
The men approached Jesus.
They put their hands on Jesus.
They seized Jesus.
They arrested Jesus.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἐπέβαλαν τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν

passages.text: And one of the bystanders drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
passages.sermon:
A group of men stood near Jesus.
One man stood among them.
This man was a bystander.
He drew his sword.
He struck the servant of the high priest.
He cut off the servant’s ear.
passages.original: εἷς δέ τις τῶν παρεστηκότων σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἔπαισεν τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτάριον

passages.text: Jesus asked the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd.
He asked them a question.
He said, “You have come out to arrest Me.
You brought swords and clubs.
You treat Me like an outlaw.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με

passages.text: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd.
He reminded them about His actions.
Every day, Jesus was with them.
He taught in the temple courts.
They did not arrest Him then.
Now, they came to arrest Him.
This happened to fulfill the Scriptures.
passages.original: καθ’ ἡμέραν ἤμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με ἀλλ’ ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαί

passages.text: Then everyone deserted Him and fled.
passages.sermon: Jesus stood before the crowd.\r\nEveryone who was with Jesus left Him.\r\nThey all ran away.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον πάντες

passages.text: One young man who had been following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth around his body. They caught hold of him, but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked.
passages.sermon:
A young man was following Jesus.
He wore only a linen cloth around his body.
Some people caught hold of him.
He left the linen cloth behind.
He ran away naked.
passages.original: Καὶ νεανίσκος τις συνηκολούθει αὐτῷ περιβεβλημένος σινδόνα ἐπὶ γυμνοῦ καὶ κρατοῦσιν αὐτόν ὁ δὲ καταλιπὼν τὴν σινδόνα γυμνὸς ἔφυγεν

passages.text: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers took Jesus.
They led Jesus to the high priest.
All the chief priests gathered there.
All the elders gathered there.
All the scribes gathered there.
They assembled together.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπήγαγον τὸν Ἰησοῦν πρὸς τὸν ἀρχιερέα καὶ συνέρχονται πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς

passages.text: Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter followed Jesus from far away.
Peter went into the courtyard of the high priest.
Peter sat with the officers.
Peter warmed himself by the fire.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ἕως ἔσω εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἦν συνκαθήμενος μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν καὶ θερμαινόμενος πρὸς τὸ φῶς

passages.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests led the religious leaders of Israel.
The Sanhedrin was the council of elders, priests, and scribes.
The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin wanted to kill Jesus.
They looked for testimony against Jesus.
They tried to find evidence to put Jesus to death.
They did not find any testimony against Him.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον ἐζήτουν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαρτυρίαν εἰς τὸ θανατῶσαι αὐτόν καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον

passages.text: For many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent.
passages.sermon:
Many people spoke falsely about Jesus.
They gave false testimony against Him.
Their statements did not agree with each other.
Their testimony was inconsistent.
passages.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἴσαι αἱ μαρτυρίαι οὐκ ἦσαν

passages.text: Then some men stood up and testified falsely against Him: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Some men stood up.
They testified falsely against Jesus.
They said, “We heard Him say this.
‘I will destroy this man-made temple.
In three days I will build another temple.
This new temple will not be made by human hands.’”
passages.original: Καί τινες ἀναστάντες ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Ὅτι Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἐγὼ καταλύσω τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον τὸν χειροποίητον καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἄλλον ἀχειροποίητον οἰκοδομήσω

passages.text: But even their testimony was inconsistent.
passages.sermon: The men gave testimony against Jesus.\r\nTheir testimony was not consistent.\r\nEven then, their statements did not agree.
passages.original: καὶ οὐδὲ οὕτως ἴση ἦν ἡ μαρτυρία αὐτῶν

passages.text: So the high priest stood up before them and questioned Jesus, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
passages.sermon:
The high priest stood up.
He went to the middle of the group.
He spoke to Jesus.
He asked Jesus a question.
He said, “Do you have no answer?”
He said, “What are these men saying against you?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς μέσον ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν λέγων Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν

passages.text: But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the high priest.
Jesus did not speak.
Jesus gave no answer.
The high priest spoke to Jesus again.
The high priest asked Jesus a question.
The high priest said, “Are you the Christ?”
The high priest said, “Are you the Son of the Blessed One?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐσιώπα καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίνατο οὐδέν Πάλιν ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Εὐλογητοῦ

passages.text: “I am,” said Jesus, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the high priest.
The high priest asked Jesus if He was the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One.
Jesus answered, “I am.”
Jesus said, “You will see the Son of Man.”
The Son of Man will sit at the right hand of Power.
The Son of Man will come with the clouds of heaven.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἐγώ εἰμι καὶ ὄψεσθε τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν καθήμενον τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “Why do we need any more witnesses?
passages.sermon:
The high priest heard Jesus speak.
The high priest tore his clothes.
The high priest spoke to the people.
He said, “Why do we need any more witnesses?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς διαρρήξας τοὺς χιτῶνας αὐτοῦ λέγει Τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων

passages.text: You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.
passages.sermon:
The high priest spoke to the council.
He said, “You have heard the blasphemy.”
He asked, “What is your verdict?”
Everyone in the council answered.
They all condemned Jesus.
They said He deserved death.
passages.original: ἠκούσατε τῆς βλασφημίας τί ὑμῖν φαίνεται Οἱ δὲ πάντες κατέκριναν αὐτὸν ἔνοχον εἶναι θανάτου

passages.text: Then some of them began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers received Him with slaps in His face.
passages.sermon:
Some men stood near Jesus.
They began to spit on Jesus.
They covered Jesus’ face with a cloth.
They hit Jesus with their fists.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Prophesy!”
The officers took Jesus.
The officers slapped Jesus on the face.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤρξαντό τινες ἐμπτύειν αὐτῷ καὶ περικαλύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ κολαφίζειν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ Προφήτευσον καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ῥαπίσμασιν αὐτὸν ἔλαβον

passages.text: While Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the servant girls of the high priest came down and saw him warming himself there. She looked at Peter and said, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was in the courtyard below.
A servant girl of the high priest came down.
She saw Peter warming himself.
She looked closely at Peter.
She said to him, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὄντος τοῦ Πέτρου κάτω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ ἔρχεται μία τῶν παιδισκῶν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον θερμαινόμενον ἐμβλέψασα αὐτῷ λέγει Καὶ σὺ μετὰ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ ἦσθα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: But he denied it. “I do not know or even understand what you are talking about,” he said. Then he went out to the gateway, and the rooster crowed.
passages.sermon:
Peter was in the courtyard below.
A servant girl of the high priest saw him.
She said, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Peter denied it.
He said, “I do not know what you are talking about.”
He said, “I do not understand what you are saying.”
Peter went out to the gateway.
The rooster crowed.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο λέγων Οὔτε οἶδα οὔτε ἐπίσταμαι σὺ τί λέγεις καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω εἰς τὸ προαύλιον καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν

passages.text: There the servant girl saw him and again said to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
passages.sermon:
A servant girl saw Peter.
She recognized him.
She spoke to the people standing nearby.
She said, “This man is one of them.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἡ παιδίσκη ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἤρξατο πάλιν λέγειν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν ὅτι Οὗτος ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐστιν

passages.text: But he denied it again. After a little while, those standing nearby said once more to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter denied it again.
Some people stood nearby.
After a little while, they spoke to Peter again.
They said to Peter, “Surely you are one of them.”
They said, “You are a Galilean too.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ πάλιν ἠρνεῖτο Καὶ μετὰ μικρὸν πάλιν οἱ παρεστῶτες ἔλεγον τῷ Πέτρῳ Ἀληθῶς ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖος εἶ

passages.text: But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter began to curse.
Peter began to swear.
Peter said, “I do not know this man.”
Peter spoke about Jesus.
Peter denied knowing Jesus to the people nearby.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἤρξατο ἀναθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύναι ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὃν λέγετε

passages.text: And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter denied knowing Jesus three times.
Immediately, the rooster crowed a second time.
Peter heard the rooster.
Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him.
Jesus had told Peter, “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
Peter realized he had denied Jesus just as Jesus said.
Peter broke down.
Peter wept.
passages.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ δευτέρου ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν Καὶ ἀνεμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τὸ ῥῆμα ὡς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα δὶς φωνῆσαι τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ καὶ ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν
